subject.title: Feature: Add denylist support for exec-approvals

question: What native exec-approvals deny policy should OpenClaw support for command and argument matches under otherwise permissive exec settings?
rationale: The choice changes a core execution security boundary and persisted config/API surface, and current open PRs encode different prompt, block, and scope semantics that automation should not choose unilaterally.

options.title: Review direct denylist PR
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/92456 as the main candidate and require protocol, prompt-parity, docs, upgrade, and live approval proof before merge.

options.title: Land path-deny separately
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/88075 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/74379 as narrower sensitive-path hardening while keeping command/content denylist policy open here.

options.title: Reject native denylist mode
options.body: Close the direction only if maintainers decide allow-everything-except policies should remain external plugin or policy-engine territory rather than core exec approvals behavior.

recommendation.title: Review direct denylist PR
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/92456 as the main candidate and require protocol, prompt-parity, docs, upgrade, and live approval proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current review and history signal on the exec approvals policy surface and already framed the maintainer decision space on this issue.
